about.title: San Jacinto Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: San Jacinto's mix of agriculture, warehousing, retail, and construction work along corridors like State Street and Ramona Expressway means workplace injuries happen in plenty of different settings, from loading docks to job sites near San Jacinto Avenue. Most workers hurt on the job in California go through the workers' compensation system, which pays medical care and partial wage replacement regardless of who caused the accident. But workers' comp isn't always the whole story. If a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate claim against that third party. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly. Instead, we connect injured San Jacinto workers with an independent attorney who can look at the details, explain what workers' comp covers, and flag whether a third-party claim might apply. There's no cost to get that conversation started.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your San Jacinto Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it doesn't rule out a claim against a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker.

items.title: Timing Matters on Two Fronts
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, while any third-party injury claim carries its own two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an on-the-job injury, so raising a claim shouldn't cost you your job.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if my employer says the accident was my fault?
items.answer: Yes. California workers' compensation generally covers injuries regardless of who was at fault, including the injured worker. An attorney can help you understand how that applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What if someone other than my employer caused my injury near a busy road like Ramona Expressway?
items.answer: If a delivery driver, contractor, or another business contributed to your workplace injury, you may have a separate third-party claim in addition to workers' comp. That claim follows California's two-year filing deadline, so it's worth discussing sooner rather than later.

items.question: How does LawProactive work if I've been hurt at a San Jacinto job site?
items.answer: LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney familiar with California workplace injury and third-party claims. We don't charge you anything and we're not the law firm handling your case — we simply make the introduction.
